value.change_explanation: The repairs separate literal query scope from factual premises, use the query year as an argument rather than asking the reader to reconstruct it, and parameterize participant-specific factual questions. The §151(d)(3)(B) percentage now consumes a stipulated §68(b) amount directly and no longer depends on §68(f) or the 2018–2025 exemption suspension. Section 151(d)(2) now executes the acquired §151(a) connection from an expressly stated exemption entitlement to an allowable deduction. Expressly stipulated dependent or qualifying-child statuses are consumed as legal intermediate premises, while the native claim remains excluded by the host's evidence check. Unrecognized relationship strings and absent dependency propositions remain unresolved instead of becoming false, and married-separate status is no longer defaulted to false.

unit_updates.property: the applicable phaseout percentage, expressed as percentage points from 0 through 100
unit_updates.quote: For purposes of subparagraph (A), the term "applicable percentage" means 2 percentage points for each $2,500 (or fraction thereof) by which the taxpayer's adjusted gross income for the taxable year exceeds the applicable amount in effect under section 68(b). In the case of a married individual filing a separate return, the preceding sentence shall be applied by substituting "$1,250" for "$2,500". In no event shall the applicable percentage exceed 100 percent.
In the case of a taxable year beginning after December 31, 2017, and before January 1, 2026, the term "exemption amount" means zero.

unit_updates.property: whether the identified individual is the taxpayer's qualifying child
unit_updates.quote:
The term "qualifying child" means, with respect to any taxpayer for any taxable year, an individual-

        (A) who bears a relationship to the taxpayer described in paragraph (2),

        (B) who has the same principal place of abode as the taxpayer for more than one-half of such taxable year,

        (C) who meets the age requirements of paragraph (3), and

        (E) who has not filed a joint return (other than only for a claim of refund) with the individual's spouse for the taxable year beginning in the calendar year in which the taxable year of the taxpayer begins.

unit_updates.property: whether the identified individual is the taxpayer's qualifying relative
unit_updates.quote:
The term "qualifying relative" means, with respect to any taxpayer for any taxable year, an individual-

        (A) who bears a relationship to the taxpayer described in paragraph (2),

        (B) who has no income for the calendar year in which such taxable year begins, and

        (D) who is not a qualifying child of such taxpayer or of any other taxpayer for any taxable year beginning in the calendar year in which such taxable year begins.

fields.question: Was {taxpayer_name} filing jointly, a surviving spouse, head of household, unmarried, or married filing separately for {query_year}?

unit_updates.property: the applicable amount determined by filing status
unit_updates.quote:
For purposes of this section, the term "applicable amount" means-

        (A) $300,000 in the case of a joint return or a surviving spouse (as defined in section 2(a)),

        (B) $275,000 in the case of a head of household (as defined in section 2(b)),

        (C) $250,000 in the case of an individual who is not married and who is not a surviving spouse or head of household, and

        (D) 1/2 the amount applicable under subparagraph (A) in the case of a married individual filing a separate return.

unit_updates.property: whether §68 applies for the taxable year
unit_updates.quote: This section shall not apply to any taxable year beginning after December 31, 2017, and before January 1, 2026.

unresolved: A negative exemption-entitlement premise alone does not prove that no §151 deduction was allowable; absent a direct negative deduction premise, §151(d)(2) remains unknown.
Relationship descriptions outside the source-backed recognized vocabulary remain unknown unless the complete household-member route is established.
The filing-status fallback recognizes only explicit statutory-category wording; an unfamiliar filing-status string remains unresolved.
A stipulated qualifying-child or dependent status is consumed only when supplied as a facts-supported case premise; question-only occurrences remain unusable.
